html:
Haitian Vodou is the religion that grew among enslaved Africans in Saint-Domingue in the 1700s. It joins the faiths of the Fon, Yoruba and Kongo peoples with elements of Catholicism.

Believers serve a distant creator and many spirits, the lwa, through song, drumming, dance and possession, led by priests and priestesses. Saints' images often stand for the lwa.

Vodou helped bind the rebels of the Bois Caiman ceremony and the revolution. The Church and the state long persecuted it, and Hollywood turned it into a byword for black magic. In 2003 Haiti recognised it as an official religion. It shares roots with Vodun in Benin and Santeria in Cuba.
sum: Haitian Vodou is the religion that grew among enslaved Africans in Saint-Domingue in the 1700s. It joins the faiths of the Fon, Yoruba and Kongo peoples with elements of Catholicism.
